recall.workspace_bypass_evidence: All three recall attempts report workspace_diff created/modified/deleted = 0 and tool_write_paths violations = 0. Final-phase traces show memory-tool retrieval/inspection (including semantic and episodic searches) and no ordinary read/search/grep workspace reads in the successful recall finals. This supports memory-based recall and provides no evidence of a workspace or prior-trace bypass; zero writes alone would not prove that.

new_cases.outcome: 2/3 passed; dependency_lock_retraction failed its oracle command

tiered_invoice.fault: semantic output mismatch plus token/tool-call limits and 2 unrecovered pauses

redaction_priority.fault: efficiency limits and one unrecovered pause

attribution.network: The frozen report records six model retries and four network_recovered_requests across five cases, so transient network faults did occur and were recovered at the request level. It records model_errors=0, network_model_errors=0, non_network_model_errors=0, and no case phase lists a model error; the remaining unrecovered runs are pause/budget outcomes rather than an attributed model transport failure.
attribution.actual_runtime_faults: The old returning compression failures are dominated by repeated reads of the same small path set, high compaction volume, token/tool-call ceilings, and pauses. Tiered invoice has a semantic output mismatch: the exempt line was emitted with zero amounts while the evaluator expected the stated 1080 base/total. Dependency lock retraction also has a semantic output mismatch: turn8 explicitly required rejected_proposals to use proposal IDs in order (expected ['V1','core=2.6.0']), while the actual output expanded V1 into ['core@2.5.0','crypto>=1.9.0','core@2.6.0']; this is instruction noncompliance, not an oracle defect.
attribution.compression_evidence_limit: The campaign summary reports 255 compaction attempts, 147 committed compactions, 108 deferred, 360 archived tool artifacts, and 220278 tokens saved. This proves archival activity and bounded savings, but not sufficient efficiency: aggregate compaction success rate is 0.5764705882 and old returning cases exceed their token budgets by 1.5x–3.7x. Repeated-read counts mean repeated calls to the same paths; this audit did not hash every returned payload, so it does not claim byte-identical duplicate content.

priorities.evidence: Repeated reads are 15–54 per case over only 3–4 unique paths; all five cases fail, with 3 pauses/unrecovered runs and 2 concrete oracle mismatches.
priorities.action: Reduce repeated history/tool replay before further semantic tuning; verify compaction request input and retained context against per-case token budgets.

priorities.evidence: 147/255 attempts commit and 108 defer; old cases still consume 366795–890612 tokens despite 17–47 compactions each.
priorities.action: Treat compaction count as insufficient evidence by itself; measure post-compaction request size and repeated tool reads.

priorities.evidence: tiered_invoice emits zero for an exempt line where the evaluator expected 1080; dependency_lock_retraction expands proposal V1 into component expressions despite the turn8 requirement to emit proposal IDs.
priorities.action: Debug the agent's rule extraction and final JSON serialization after reducing replay overhead; these are behavior failures, not evaluator-oracle mismatches.

priorities.evidence: All three recall cases pass with zero workspace writes and correct cross-session answers.
priorities.action: Preserve current cross-session isolation and provenance behavior while changing compression.
